thread:
maria: heads up — noticed a weird queue stall in us-west1 gpupool. small short jobs are sitting at the front and preventing medium/long jobs from scheduling :facepalm:
aj: can you paste the admission debug logs? which scheduler version?
maria: scheduler v2.18.1. here's the snippet from admission controller (trimmed):
```
I0321 15:02:12 admission.go:234 Admit request job=job-1432 resources=[gpu:1] pool=us-west1-gpu short=true
I0321 15:02:12 queue.go:89 enqueued job-1432 pos=1
I0321 15:02:15 admit.go:412 allocate tried gang=true, preempt=false
I0321 15:02:15 dispatch.go:58 dispatch blocked head=job-1432 reason=allocation-failed
```
maria: you can see a bunch of medium jobs behind job-1432 waiting but the allocator never tries preempt or fallback variants.
ben: that smells like the admission path failing to set can_preempt=true for small ephemeral jobs when they're part of a gang. we saw a related regression in canary two weeks ago.
aj: thanks. can you grab p99 scheduling latency from graphite for the last hour? also any notable pod eviction events?
maria: p99 spiked to ~12s about 15:01 and then a big queue tail at 15:02. no evictions logged.
sam: infra-bot just posted region capacity warnings earlier for us-west1 — GPU utilization was 98% around 15:00. might be tight enough that the scheduler gave up trying fallbacks.
infra-bot: [alert] us-west1 GPU pool saturation > 95% for 10m — writeup at https://internal.ops/reports/us-west1-sat
tara: could be two issues: (1) admission preempt flip regression (2) resource tagging mismatch causing the allocator to think the medium jobs require a different SKU. either can create front-locking.
ben: agree. quick triage: reproduce locally with a synthetic workload of short high-priority jobs + medium jobs, watch admission.can_preempt logic.
aj: workaround for now: bump the preemption throttle config to be more aggressive and enable fallback_to_quantized_model=true on affected routes — that will let the medium jobs fall back to a compatible variant if exact SKU isn't free.
sam: can we do a rolling restart of scheduler v2.18.1 in us-west1 to pick up the last fix? risk is brief admission hiccups but might clear the locked head.
maria: i'm running a graceful restart on one scheduler replica now. monitoring queues.
aj: also temporarily increase max_concurrent_short_jobs_per_pool from 50 -> 80 to avoid small-job pileups; revert after root cause. note this increases transient cost.
tara: cost note logged — bumping limit will add ~2-3% to hourly GPU spend if sustained. filing a quick ticket to finance ops.
ben: log from the restarted replica shows allocator now marking can_preempt=true for the earlier pattern and several waiting jobs were admitted within 30s.
maria: queues cleared around 15:06. medium jobs started running.
sam: follow up items: 1) create regression test for can_preempt w/ gang=true, 2) add metric for 'head_block_duration' per pool, 3) backport the admission fix to 2.18.0 branch.
aj: +1 on tests and metric. add a cheap alert: head_block_duration > 60s -> paging oncall.
infra-bot: [note] incident created: INC-2026-443 us-west1 queue head blocking. linked runbook: https://internal.runbooks/queue-headlock
mar ia: thanks everyone. leaving a short postmortem soon with timeline and cost delta from the throttle bump. :+1:
